findings.passage: In South Carolina, when someone attempts to vote, he or she must provide a valid and current photo ID. I believe that such is necessary to ensure the integrity of our electoral process.
findings.note: Voter ID section of the senator's own official site. The page shows no date; date given is the date fetched, so the precision is marked unknown. He states the photo ID rule and says he believes it is necessary for election integrity.

findings.passage: “A voter ID requirement strengthens voters’ rights by protecting the votes of all who vote legally,” writes Matthew Rousu, Professor of Economics at Susquehanna University for Forbes. “When voter fraud occurs, it dilutes and weakens the votes of all law-abiding voters. One could make a reasonable argument that by not forcing identification and encouraging fraud, you are violating the promise of one person, one vote.”  He is absolutely right.
findings.note: Same page: he quotes a Forbes column on voter ID and adds that the writer is right. Page shows no date; date given is the date fetched.
